correctness.rationale: The base-b=n-1 signed residue-sum vector satisfies S(bx)=B S(x), with B_(r,s)=a_(r+s mod n), a_d=(-1)^d for d<=n-2 and a_(n-1)=0. For n odd Fourier characters v_z (z^n=1) satisfy B v_z=A(z) v_(z^-1) with A(z)=sum_{d=0}^{n-2}(-z)^d; hence B² has eigenvalue 0 for z=1 and -((z-1)/(z+1))² otherwise. The odd-binomial polynomial P_n(Y)=sum_{j=0}^{(n-1)/2}(-1)^j binom(n,2j+1)Y^j vanishes on all nonconstant eigenvalues by ((1+w)^n-(1-w)^n)/(2w) and equals n at 0. Consequently P_n(B²)=J_n, and multiplying S(x) proves the conjectured all-residue relation for every odd n>=3 and integer x>=0. Sum of digit signs cancels in consecutive pairs since b even, yielding the parity endpoint. Independently verified exact integer P_n(B²)=J_n for n=3,5,7,9.
